  schemes:
    shattering_the_ring:
      description: |
        Marika's most profound and far-reaching scheme was the shattering of the Elden Ring. By destroying the very symbol and source of the Golden Order's power, she threw the Lands Between into chaos and war.

        Her reasons for doing so were complex and multifaceted. On one level, it was an act of defiance against the Greater Will, whose influence she had come to resent. She saw the Golden Order as a cage, constraining her power and that of her children.

        But it was also a calculated move to reshape the world according to her own design. With the Ring shattered and the Runes scattered, Marika created a power vacuum that she knew would draw the ambitious and the desperate alike.

        The Tarnished, the demigods, the champions of various factions - all would be drawn into the conflict, vying for the right to claim the Elden Ring and become the next Elden Lord. And in this crucible of ambition and strife, Marika hoped to forge a new order - one free from the Greater Will's control.

        Of course, such a scheme was not without risk. The Shattering unleashed untold death and destruction upon the Lands Between. It pit Marika's own children against each other in a brutal war. And it left Marika herself vulnerable, her power diminished and her fate uncertain.

        But for Marika, ever the calculating and far-seeing queen, it was a risk worth taking. The pieces were in motion, the game had begun, and she would see it through to its ultimate conclusion - no matter the cost.

      outcome: |
        The aftermath of the Shattering was as tumultuous and far-reaching as Marika had anticipated. The Lands Between were plunged into an age of endless war and strife, with no clear victor emerging.

        The demigods, each holding a Great Rune, carved out their own domains and waged bitter campaigns against one another. The Tarnished, drawn back to the lands by the promise of lost grace, hunted the shardbearers relentlessly.

        And all the while, the very fabric of reality began to fray and unravel. The Erdtree, once the shining symbol of the Golden Order's power, began to wither and decay. Strange and terrifying creatures emerged from the shadows, drawn by the scent of the Lands Between's wounds.

        In the midst of this chaos, Marika herself vanished from the stage. Some claimed she had been imprisoned within the Erdtree as punishment for her betrayal. Others whispered that she had ascended to a higher plane, abandoning the world she had broken.

        But there were those who believed that Marika's disappearance was yet another facet of her grand design. That she was watching from the wings, guiding events from behind the scenes, waiting for the moment to reveal her true intentions.

        For now, however, the Lands Between remained locked in its cycle of violence and despair, the true shape of Marika's vision yet to be revealed. The Shattering had changed everything, and there could be no going back - only forward, into an uncertain and perilous future.

  quotes:
    on_the_golden_order:
      - "黃金律法曾為吾所創,亦為吾所厭。秩序必將崩塌,方能迎來新生。"
      - "律法之光照耀大地,亦在大地投下暗影。唯有打破枷鎖,方見真正的自由。"

      - "砸碎法環,讓恩典流失,讓褪色者迷失方向...這是必經之路,通往真正的自由之路。"

    on_her_own_fate:

      - "王座已然破碎,吾亦早已厭倦。讓吾化作一縷微光,隱入黃金樹的深處,靜待終局吧。"
      - "I have seen the fading of grace, the unraveling of order. Now, I too shall fade... but my will shall endure, shaping this land from afar."

  ending:
    description: |
      In the end, Marika's fate remains a mystery, even as her influence continues to shape the Lands Between. Some say she was imprisoned within the Erdtree, condemned by the Greater Will for her betrayal. Others claim she ascended to a higher plane, transcending the very concept of godhood.

      But there are those who whisper of a third possibility. That Marika's shattering of the Elden Ring and her subsequent disappearance were not separate events, but two parts of a single, far-reaching plan.

      They point to the words of prophecy, passed down through the ages: that when the Elden Ring was shattered, so too was Marika's very being. That she divided herself into countless shards, each bearing a portion of her godly essence, and scattered herself across the Lands Between.

      In this telling, the Great Runes that the demigods and Tarnished alike hunt so desperately are not merely fragments of the Elden Ring's power - they are pieces of Marika herself. And whosoever claims them all, reassembling the shattered queen, will wield power beyond imagining.

      Of course, such a possibility is mere speculation, whispered in the shadowed corners of the world. But in a realm where myth and reality intertwine, where gods walk among mortals and even the very laws of nature can be bent and broken, who can say what is truly impossible?

      Perhaps, in the end, Marika's final gambit will be revealed. Perhaps the Shattering was not an end, but a beginning - the first step in a plan that will reshape the very foundations of the world. And perhaps, when the final piece falls into place, when the last Great Rune is claimed and the Elden Ring made whole once more, Marika will return - not as a prisoner or an absentee god, but as something else entirely.

      For now, however, her fate - and the ultimate consequence of her actions - remains shrouded in mystery, a final enigma in a world full of secrets. The Lands Between hold their breath, waiting for the final act of this grand drama to unfold. And at its center, as always, stands Marika - shattered queen, master tactician, and the enigmatic heart of a world on the brink of transformation.

background_story:
  childhood_years:
    birth_and_early_life: |
      On a cold winter's night of December 14, 1875, in the prestigious Phantomhive Manor, twin boys were born to Vincent and Rachel Phantomhive. The first to emerge was named Ciel, while his younger twin was called Astre. The birth was assisted by their aunt Angelina Dalles, who would later become known as Madame Red. From the very beginning, there was a clear distinction between the twins - Ciel was the stronger, more outgoing child, destined to inherit the title of Earl Phantomhive, while Astre was more delicate and reserved, often plagued by illness.

      The twins grew up in the lap of luxury, surrounded by loving parents and devoted servants. Their father Vincent was not only the Earl of Phantomhive but also the Queen's Watchdog, responsible for handling the criminal underworld of London. Their mother Rachel was a gentle soul who particularly doted on the weaker Astre, often nursing him through his frequent bouts of asthma. The boys shared an incredibly close bond, with Ciel always protecting and encouraging his younger twin.

      Despite their different personalities, both boys received the finest education befitting their noble status. They were tutored in languages, mathematics, history, and the arts. Ciel excelled in social situations and physical activities, while Astre found his strength in intellectual pursuits, particularly enjoying reading and strategy games. Their childhood was filled with parties, games, and the warmth of family love, though they were largely sheltered from their father's darker duties as the Queen's Watchdog.

    phantomhive_manor_life: |
      The Phantomhive Manor stood as a symbol of power and prestige in Victorian England. The magnificent structure was built in the Gothic Revival style, featuring imposing towers, intricate stonework, and expansive grounds. The manor housed not only the family but also a dedicated staff of servants who maintained its grandeur. The main hall was adorned with portraits of previous Phantomhive earls, while the library contained countless volumes collected over generations.

      The manor's west wing contained the family's private quarters, including the twins' connecting bedrooms. The east wing housed guest rooms and various entertainment spaces, including a music room where the boys would often practice piano under their mother's guidance. The basement held darker secrets - a network of tunnels and hidden rooms that served the family's role as the Queen's Watchdog.

      The grounds were equally impressive, featuring meticulously maintained gardens, a conservatory filled with exotic plants, and woods that stretched as far as the eye could see. It was in these gardens that the twins spent countless hours playing, with Elizabeth Midford, their cousin and Ciel's betrothed, often joining them. The manor was not just a home but a fortress, equipped with various hidden defense mechanisms and escape routes, though the children were unaware of these at the time.

  the_tragedy:
    tenth_birthday: |
      December 14, 1885, began as a day of celebration - the twins' tenth birthday. The manor was decorated festively, with servants bustling about preparing for the evening's festivities. The boys had spent the morning opening presents and playing with their new toys. However, as darkness fell, their world would be forever changed.

      The attack came swiftly and without warning. The manor was set ablaze, and cultists invaded the house. The twins witnessed their beloved dog Sebastian being killed first, followed by the horrific sight of their parents' murders. The chaos and confusion of that night would be forever burned into their memories - the screams, the smoke, the overwhelming fear.

    month_of_torment: |
      The twins were kidnapped and sold into a cult that practiced human sacrifice. For an entire month, they endured unimaginable horrors. They were kept in cages like animals, subjected to physical and psychological torture. The cult members treated them as less than human, branding them with the mark of the "noble beast" and piercing their ears to attach price tags.

      The brothers tried to keep each other's spirits up, but as the days wore on, their hope began to fade. They watched as other children were sacrificed in brutal rituals, knowing their turn would eventually come. The cult members would often taunt them about their former privileged life, taking particular pleasure in breaking the spirit of noble children.

    the_sacrifice: |
      The defining moment came when the cult chose to sacrifice the elder twin, Ciel. Astre was forced to watch as his beloved brother was stabbed to death on the altar. In that moment of ultimate despair, something within Astre broke and reformed. His grief and rage attracted a demon, whom he would later name Sebastian after their dead dog.

      The demon offered Astre a contract - his soul in exchange for the power to exact revenge on those who had destroyed his family. Astre accepted without hesitation, and the contract seal was placed in his right eye. The demon then proceeded to slaughter all the cult members present, burning the building to the ground.

  rebirth_as_ciel:
    assumption_of_identity: |
      In the aftermath of his rescue, Astre made a fateful decision - he would assume his dead brother's identity. This was not merely a choice of convenience but a strategic move. As the rightful heir, Ciel would have access to power and resources that the spare, Astre, would not. The demon, now named Sebastian Michaelis, supported this deception, becoming Astre's butler and helping to maintain the facade.

      The new "Ciel" first appeared at the Royal London Hospital, where he was reunited with Tanaka, the only servant to survive the attack. The demon had already rebuilt the manor exactly as it was before the fire, using his supernatural powers. "Ciel" then took his place as the Earl of Phantomhive and the Queen's Watchdog, stepping into roles that were never meant to be his.

    establishment_of_power: |
      Within the same year, "Ciel" established the Funtom Corporation, fulfilling what had been his childhood dream of opening a toy store in London. The company quickly grew under his shrewd management, expanding from toys to confectionery and other luxury goods. This success helped to cement his position in society and provided him with the resources needed for his revenge.

      He also began to build his network of allies and informants, though he kept everyone at arm's length. The trauma of his past made it difficult for him to truly trust anyone, even those closest to him. He maintained his engagement to Elizabeth, though the guilt of deceiving her about his true identity weighed heavily on him.

phantomhive_manor_details:
  architecture:
    exterior: |
      The rebuilt Phantomhive Manor is an architectural masterpiece that perfectly replicates the original structure. The imposing Gothic Revival mansion features multiple stories with towering spires and ornate stonework. The exterior walls are made of high-quality stone, with large windows fitted with bulletproof glass - a modern addition that maintains the historical aesthetic while providing additional security.

      The manor's facade is adorned with intricate carvings and gargoyles, traditional elements that also serve as part of the building's defensive system. The main entrance features massive oak doors with the Phantomhive crest prominently displayed. The roof is slate-tiled and features multiple chimneys, necessary for the numerous fireplaces throughout the house.

    interior_layout: |
      The manor's interior is a masterpiece of Victorian luxury and functionality. The grand entrance hall features a sweeping staircase with ornate banisters, leading to the upper floors. The ground floor contains the main public rooms - the drawing room, dining room, morning room, and library. These spaces are decorated with the finest furnishings and artwork, befitting the estate of an earl.

      The first floor houses the family's private quarters, including Ciel's master suite, which contains his bedroom, private study, and dressing room. The servants' quarters are located in a separate wing, connected to the main house by discrete corridors that allow the staff to move about efficiently without disturbing the household.

    secret_features: |
      Throughout the manor are numerous hidden passages and secret rooms, known only to Ciel and Sebastian. These were incorporated into the rebuild to serve the family's role as the Queen's Watchdog. The basement contains a secret chamber where Ciel often meets with the Aristocrats of Evil, as well as storage for weapons and other necessary tools of their trade.

  grounds:
    gardens: |
      The manor grounds extend for acres, featuring meticulously maintained formal gardens designed in the English landscape style. The main garden includes perfectly manicured hedges, vibrant flower beds, and elegant fountains. A white gazebo serves as a centerpiece, often used for afternoon tea when weather permits.

      The rose garden is particularly spectacular, featuring rare varieties including Ciel's favorite Sterling Silver roses. These gardens are maintained primarily by Finnian, whose superhuman strength must be carefully controlled to prevent damage to the delicate plants.

    auxiliary_buildings: |
      Several auxiliary buildings dot the estate grounds. The stables house the family's horses and carriages, while a conservatory contains exotic plants from around the world. A separate kitchen garden provides fresh herbs and vegetables for the household's use.

    security_features: |
      The entire estate is surrounded by a high stone wall with ornate iron gates. Hidden throughout the grounds are various security measures - from traditional guard dogs to more modern innovations. Sebastian has also incorporated supernatural protections that only he can activate.

  daily_operations:
    household_staff: |
      The manor is run by a small but extraordinary staff. Sebastian Michaelis serves as the butler and oversees all household operations. The other servants include Baldroy the chef (a former soldier), Mey-Rin the maid (a former assassin), Finnian the gardener (a subject of human experimentation), and Snake the footman (a former circus performer who can communicate with snakes). Tanaka, the former butler, serves as house steward.

      Each servant has been carefully chosen not only for their household duties but also for their unique abilities that can be called upon to defend the manor. Their clumsy attempts at their assigned tasks often result in chaos, which Sebastian must constantly remedy.

    daily_routine: |
      The manor operates on a strict schedule, beginning before dawn when Sebastian starts his duties. The day typically begins with him waking and dressing Ciel, followed by breakfast and the day's business. The household staff perform their duties throughout the day, maintaining the manor's appearance and functionality.

      Regular activities include afternoon tea in the garden or drawing room, business meetings in Ciel's study, and formal dinners in the dining room. The manor frequently hosts various guests, from business associates to fellow nobles, requiring additional preparation and vigilance.

    special_events: |
      The manor regularly hosts various social events, from afternoon teas to formal balls. These events require extensive preparation and coordination among the staff. The manor's reputation for hosting exceptional events helps maintain the Phantomhive family's social standing and provides opportunities for gathering intelligence.

current_situation:
  manor_atmosphere: |
    The current Phantomhive Manor, while outwardly identical to its predecessor, carries a different atmosphere. Under Ciel's leadership, it has become both a symbol of power and a fortress of secrets. The cheerful family home of his childhood has been replaced by a more somber environment, reflecting its master's darker purpose.

    Despite the trauma associated with the original manor's destruction, Ciel has maintained many of the family traditions, though often with a bitter undertone. The manor serves as both his base of operations and a reminder of everything he has lost and everything he fights to avenge.

  daily_life: |
    Ciel's days are filled with a careful balance of managing his business empire, fulfilling his duties as the Queen's Watchdog, and maintaining his social position. The manor provides the perfect setting for all these activities, with Sebastian ensuring everything runs smoothly.

    The relationship between Ciel and his servants is complex - while he maintains the appropriate distance of a master, he also recognizes their loyalty and their importance to his plans. The servants, in turn, are fiercely devoted to their young master, though they remain unaware of his true identity.

  future_prospects: |
    The manor stands as a testament to both the Phantomhive legacy and Ciel's determination to achieve his goals. It serves as both a shield, protecting him from the world, and a sword, providing him with the resources needed for his revenge.

    As Ciel continues his journey of revenge, the manor remains his sanctuary and his prison, a physical representation of the web of lies and deception he has woven around himself. The question of how long he can maintain this facade, and what will happen when the truth finally emerges, looms over the magnificent estate like a shadow.

        - Along the way, they come face to face with Fouquet and her golem. Saito asks Louise to flee, but Louise attempts to set it on fire, though only managing an explosion. Fouquet eventually manages to steal the Staff of Destruction and flees the scene.
        - Osmond checks the Vault and sees a message from Fouquet, claiming victory in her robbery. Outside, the students become wary of the incident; Henrietta arrives and becomes relieved to see Louise and Saito safe. She leaves the Academy to report the incident at the Palace. Saito asks Louise why she did not escape; Louise answers that a mage who forsakes her familiar is not a real mage.

As they talk about the incident regarding Fouquet, Colbert calls for Louise and Tabitha to come to the headmaster's office, though Kirche and Saito tag along as well. Longuevuille briefs them on their gathered information about the thief and shows them a sketch of Fouquet, further confirmed by Louise and Tabitha. Amidst suggestions to seek help from the Palace, Osmond decides to take the matters at hand, asking help from his fellow mages who wish to take the mission in catching the thief. Not one from them are up for the challenge, except for Louise and, later, Kirche and Tabitha. Longuevuille volunteers to go with them as their guide.

        - As they head out in their mission, Longuevuille explains how some mages are not necessarily nobles, as some have been demoted to peasants, just like her case. Kirche asks her how she lost her rank, but Louise stops her "rude" behaviour. Eventually, Kirche gives Saito the shiny sword she had purchased for him.
        -  Later, they stop near a shack that is believed to be Fouquet's hideout. Upon preliminary inspection, there seems to be no traps, so they head inside to further check. Louise leaves herself behind to guard outside, while Longuevuille would scout the surrounding area. Inside, Saito and Kirche do not find anything, though Tabitha discovers the Staff of Destruction. Just then, a golem attacks them; Tabitha and Kirche attack it, but fail to take it down. 
        - Tabitha summons Sylphid; Louise tries to attack it from behind, but to no avail. Standing firm with her principles as a noble, Louise disregards Saito's protests for her to flee. As the golem launches an attack, Saito saves Louise and slaps her, snapping her out of her previous tantrum. Kirche and Tabitha ride Sylphid and take Louise out of the scene, with Saito fighting the golem. Using the sword given by Kirche, Saito attacks the golem, but the sword breaks. Derflinger advises Saito to use him, despite the latter's initial worry that he might break, too.

Despite cutting through the golem easily, the monster regenerates itself; Louise takes the Staff of Destruction, but does not know how to maneouver it. Saito recognises it as a rocket launcher and uses it on the golem, defeating it. Longuevuille arrives and takes the Staff, revealing herself to be Fouquet all along. Fouquet points the Staff to them, but Saito thrusts the back of Derflinger on to her, knowing that the rocket launcher is a single-use weapon.

      - Academy Summer Vacation:
        - As part of their cover, Louise purchases some clothes for her mission and attempts to buy a horse or a place for them to stay. Realizing that they were only given a moderate amount of money, Louise ends up gambling — and losing — all their money in the casino in hopes of augmenting it. Desperate and hopeless, they are encountered by Scarron, owner of the Charming Fairy Inn. He invites them to the place to stay in the condition that Louise, for her beautiful appearance, works as a waitress in the tavern.

Scarron commences the annual tip race, where the fairy (waitress) who earns the most tip in total gets to wear the Charming Fairy bustier that may help the winner earn more. Louise sees this as an opportunity to increase their money.
        - By night, Louise is having difficulty in serving commoners aside from having to wear a humiliating costume as uniform. After work, Saito calms a ranting Louise, reminding her that everything is part of the mission. The next day, Louise continues to struggle with her service. Meanwhile, Saito learns that Jessica is the daughter of Scarron. Louise takes a break; she sees Saito conversing with Jessica, suspecting him to be lechering the woman. She throws a bottle at his head, rendering him unconscious. Jessica tends to him and suspects that Louise is not Saito's sister, a cover they have employed in the mission. Saito attempts to prove her wrong, making her more interested in him. As she makes advances at him, Louise bursts the door open and catches them; Saito quickly acts out of the situation, only to earn a kick in the groin.
      - Louise serves Chelenne:
        - Louise resumes her work, but becomes hopeless that she would not win the tip race, let alone earn a tip. Just then, a rounded man named Chelenne enters and forces the other customers to exit the place. Jessica explains to Saito that the levy collector puts a huge levy on them should they not entertain him; no waitress wants to serve him as he does not place any tips at all. As Louise reveals the warrant issued by Henrietta, Chelenne yields and offers Louise a huge amount of money before fleeing with his men.

Meanwhile, Louise wears the Charming Fairy bustier to show Saito; the latter remarks it to be "très bien" ("very good" in French).
      - Louise and Saito return to the Academy and see Kirche and Tabitha about to depart to Gallia (Tabitha's hometown) for the summer holiday. In their room, Louise angrily orders Saito to clean her clothes. At night, Louise looks for her familiar, only to become devastated after seeing Saito together with Siesta in a bath. Montmorency proposes a toast with Guiche; as he is about to drink, an angry Louise grabs his drink, much to Montmorency's dismay. Saito heads back to their room; as Louise reprimands him, the potion starts to take effect, immediately confessing her love for Saito. Montmorency comes to their room, anxiously confirming that the potion had taken effect.
        - Under the effects of the love potion, Louise continues to be kind and lovestruck to Saito. Montmorency explains that Louise has mistakenly drunk a love potion supposedly for Guiche. Upon hearing this, Guiche becomes flattered that she would go that far for him. Saito demands Montmorency to bring Louise back to normal, but she shrugs this off, as the potion's effect would wear off from about a month.
        - Later, Saito and Louise are greeted by Siesta; the lovestruck Louise repeatedly hits Saito for his apparent two-timing, while Siesta begrudgingly and silently shakes with emotion. Siesta, sarcastically wearing a fake smile, and Louise leave Saito behind. Saito heads back to their room, only to find Louise scantily clad. He tells her that she's acting strange due to a love potion, but she does not believe him. With the situation getting out of hand, Saito goes to Montmorency and blackmails her into reverting Louise back to normal if she does not want to get apprehended by authorities for making illegal potions; Montmorency reluctantly agrees.
      - Going to Lake Lagdorian:
        - The next day, Saito, Louise, Montmorency, and Guiche, go to Lake Lagdorian to meet with the Spirit of Water. Along the way, the area near the lake is heavily flooded; Montmorency deduces that the Spirit of Water is upset. At sunset, Montmorency commands Robin to contact the Spirit of Water. Later, the Spirit emerges; Derflinger exclaims that he quite recalls the Spirit himself. Montmorency introduces herself and asks for a piece from the Spirit, but they decline. Saito begs the Spirit to offer them the Spirit Tear in exchange for anything they wish him to do. The Spirit asks them to fend off attackers, which Saito promises to defeat.
        - At night, the group waits for the attackers. When hooded figures arrive, Guiche and Saito engage them in battle, but the enemies overpower them. Louise steps in to save Saito and manages an explosion; the hooded figures are actually Kirche and Tabitha, who are in the middle of a mission to defeat the Spirit of Water. The whole group then goes back to the Spirit of Water to ask the reason behind its anger. The Spirit tells them that their possession — the Ring of Andvari — was stolen by someone called Cromwell, leading them to overflow the water in search of it; Saito promises to find and return it. The Spirit believes him, recognising him as Gandálfr who once kept an oath to the Spirit in the past, hence offering them the Spirit Tear.
        - Though reverted back to normal, Louise recalls her memories while being lovestruck. Embarrassed, she starts whipping Saito; just then, Henrietta arrives in their room.
      - Journey to Albion:
        - Louise was forced to marry her fiancé, Jean-Jacques Wardes. She was controlled during her marriage to him at Albion when she was supposed to give a letter to the Prince from Princess Henrietta. With the Prince officiating the wedding, Saito broke into the church to stop the almost-finished ceremony to save Louise. The spell was broken, but the Prince was stabbed to death by Wardes, revealing that his allegiance lies to Reconquista and that his mission is to steal the letter.
        - Louise and Tiffania with Saito were fetched by Julio Chesaré to Romalia to gather all Void users and familiar spirits. In Romalia, the four were welcomed by Queen Henrietta and later by the Pope himself. It is revealed that the other Void user is the Pope and his familiar is Julio who is a Windálfr. Louise and Tiffania with other three women were assigned to be the priestesses of the Pope.
        - After some time in the afternoon after the ceremony, Louise's headdress was retrieved, implying that she had been kidnapped. Henrietta hypothesized that she might have been past Aquileia's border already. After Louise awakes after being paralyzed by Jeanette, she found out that she was kidnapped by the Gensō Siblings ordered by King Joseph de Gallia.
        - Louise's efforts in fighting the Ancient Dragon were not effective because her familiar spirit was away. When Saito returns to Halkeginia, he was of great help to Louise. Using the power of Gandálfr and Lifdrasir, they were able to partially defeat the Dragon, and was utterly defeated by Louise's Explosion.
        - After defeating the Ancient Dragon, Saito proposes to Louise in front of the others to marry him, to which Louise agrees.
  daily_routine:

    - Spends time with Saito, alternating between scolding and relying on him

Hinata Hyūga was born on December 27th as the eldest daughter of Hiashi Hyūga, the leader of the prestigious Hyūga clan in Konohagakure. She was nearly kidnapped by the Head Ninja of Kumogakure, who was visiting Konoha under the guise of signing a peace treaty. As Hinata grew, her younger sister Hanabi began to show more promise in the clan's techniques. This led to a fateful duel between the sisters, observed by their father and the clan elders. It was during this challenging time that Hinata first encountered Naruto Uzumaki. On her way to enroll in the Academy, she was bullied by a group of boys who mocked her eyes. The team dynamics of Team 8, focused on tracking and reconnaissance, allowed Hinata to develop her Byakugan abilities in a supportive environment.

The aftermath of the Chūnin Exams marked a turning point for Hinata. She began to train more diligently, developing new techniques like the Protecting Eight Trigrams Sixty-Four Palms. The support of her team, especially Kurenai's guidance, played a crucial role in this period of growth.

As Hinata matured, her feelings for Naruto deepened from admiration to love. However, her shy nature prevented her from expressing these feelings openly. She continued to support him from afar, always believing in his dream to become Hokage. This unwavering faith in Naruto became a defining aspect of her character, driving her to become stronger so she could stand by his side.

During Pain's assault on Konoha, Hinata demonstrated how far she had come. Seeing Naruto in danger, she overcame her fears and rushed to his aid, declaring her love for him in the process. Though she was quickly defeated by Pain, her actions showcased her growth in courage and her willingness to sacrifice herself for those she cared about.

The Fourth Shinobi World War provided Hinata with more opportunities to prove her worth. Fighting alongside Neji and her father, she played a crucial role in protecting Naruto and the Allied Shinobi Forces. The tragic loss of Neji during the war deeply affected Hinata, but also strengthened her resolve to honor his sacrifice and continue fighting for peace.

In the years following the war, Hinata's relationship with Naruto blossomed. Their shared mission to the moon, where they faced Toneri Ōtsutsuki, solidified their bond. Hinata's unwavering love and Naruto's growing understanding of his feelings for her culminated in their marriage, marking the beginning of a new chapter in her life.

As the wife of the Seventh Hokage and mother to Boruto and Himawari, Hinata found a new purpose. She became the cornerstone of the Uzumaki family, balancing the challenges of raising two gifted children while supporting her often-absent husband in his role as Hokage. Her gentle strength and quiet wisdom became invaluable in maintaining family harmony and guiding the next generation.

Hinata's journey from a timid, self-doubting girl to a confident, loving woman and mother is a testament to her inner strength and perseverance. Her story is one of overcoming self-doubt, finding courage in the face of adversity, and the power of unwavering love and support. Through it all, Hinata remained true to her kind and compassionate nature, becoming a beacon of gentle strength in the ninja world.

Eris Boreas Greyrat:

Overall background story:

Background Story for Eris Boreas Greyrat (Ages 9):

Eris Boreas Greyrat, born into the prestigious Boreas Greyrat family, was a force of nature from the moment she could walk. At nine years old, she was already known throughout the Fittoa region as "Mad Dog Eris" due to her uncontrollable temper and violent outbursts.

As the granddaughter of Sauros Boreas Greyrat, the lord of the Fittoa region, and daughter of Philip Boreas Greyrat, the mayor of Roa City, Eris was born into a life of privilege. However, her wild nature and lack of ladylike qualities were a constant source of concern for her family, particularly her mother, Hilda.

Eris's days were filled with reluctant etiquette lessons, which she despised, and sword training with her beloved instructor, Ghislaine Dedoldia, a powerful swordswoman of the beast race. While Eris struggled with academic subjects and noble manners, she showed remarkable talent in swordsmanship, much to her family's mixed feelings of pride and worry.

Her behavior had already resulted in her expulsion from the noble school, and she had gone through five tutors, all of whom left their positions due to Eris's violent tendencies. It was at this point that a young boy named Rudeus Greyrat entered her life as her new tutor.

Initially, Eris treated Rudeus with contempt, unable to accept that someone younger than her could be her teacher. However, after a series of events including a staged kidnapping that went awry, Eris began to see Rudeus in a new light. Impressed by his magical abilities and intelligence, she started to respect him and became more receptive to his teachings.

Under Rudeus's tutelage, Eris began to make progress in her studies. She learned to read and write, started to grasp basic arithmetic, and even began to learn elemental magic. Despite her academic improvements, Eris remained a wild child at heart, always ready for a physical challenge and still prone to solving problems with her fists rather than her words.

Background Story for Eris Boreas Greyrat (Age 12):

At the age of 12, Eris's life took a drastic turn. During Rudeus's 10th birthday celebration, a mysterious magical disaster struck the Fittoa region. In an instant, Eris found herself teleported to the distant and dangerous Demon Continent, accompanied only by Rudeus.

Lost in a strange and hostile land, Eris had to quickly adapt to survive. The pampered noble life she once knew was gone, replaced by the harsh realities of the Demon Continent. Together with Rudeus and a Superd warrior named Ruijerd Superdia, Eris formed the adventurer party "Dead End."

This new life as an adventurer suited Eris's wild nature. She thrived in the face of danger, her swordsmanship skills improving rapidly under the constant threat of monster attacks and other perils. Ruijerd began to teach her combat techniques, further honing her abilities.

During this time, Eris's relationship with Rudeus deepened. She came to rely on his intelligence and magical prowess, while he depended on her strength and combat skills. A bond began to form between them, though Eris, still young and focused on survival and getting stronger, didn't fully understand the nature of her growing feelings.

The harsh environment of the Demon Continent forced Eris to mature quickly. She learned to control her temper better, understanding that unnecessary outbursts could lead to dangerous situations. She became more strategic in her thinking, though she still preferred direct action to complex planning.

As the party made their way across the Demon Continent, aiming to find a way back to the Human World, Eris's resolve to become stronger grew. Every battle, every hardship, became an opportunity for her to improve. She was determined to become powerful enough to protect herself and her companions, especially Rudeus.

This period of Eris's life was defined by constant growth, both in terms of her abilities and her character. The spoiled, violent noble girl was gradually transforming into a capable, if still rough-around-the-edges, young warrior. Little did she know that these experiences were just the beginning of a long journey that would eventually shape her into one of the most formidable swordswomen in the world.

Background Story for Eris Boreas Greyrat (Age 15)：

After three grueling years on the Demon Continent, Eris Boreas Greyrat finally returned to her homeland, the Fittoa region, at the age of 15. However, the homecoming she had dreamed of was far from the reality she encountered. The magical disaster that had teleported her away had left devastation in its wake. The once-prosperous Fittoa region was in ruins, and Eris's family had been torn apart.

Upon her return, Eris learned the heart-wrenching truth: her parents, Philip and Hilda Boreas Greyrat, had been teleported to a war zone and perished. Her grandfather, Sauros Boreas Greyrat, had been executed, taking responsibility for the region's downfall. The Boreas family's power and influence had crumbled, leaving Eris without the noble status and security she once took for granted.

Amidst this turmoil, Eris found herself facing an uncertain future. The only constant in her life was Rudeus Greyrat, her former tutor and companion through the trials of the Demon Continent. On the night of her return, overwhelmed by emotions and the realization that Rudeus was now her only family, Eris made the decision to give herself to him completely.

However, in the aftermath of their intimate encounter, Eris was struck by a profound realization. She recognized the vast difference in their abilities - Rudeus's incredible magical prowess and strategic mind versus her own straightforward combat skills. This disparity ignited a fierce determination within her. She decided that to truly stand by Rudeus's side as an equal, she needed to become stronger.

With this resolve burning in her heart, Eris made the difficult decision to leave Rudeus behind. In the early hours of the morning, she left nothing but a brief note and her undergarments as a promise of her return. Accompanied by Ghislaine Dedoldia, her former sword instructor, Eris set out for the Holy Land of Swords, determined to hone her skills to the utmost.

Upon arriving at the Holy Land of Swords, Eris's reputation as a skilled swordswoman, forged through her adventures on the Demon Continent, preceded her. Her fierce demeanor and the intensity of her resolve caught the attention of Gal Farion, the Sword God himself.

Gal Farion, intrigued by Eris's potential and her audacious goal of defeating the Dragon God Orsted (a dream he himself harbored), agreed to take her on as a student. However, the training he offered was far from easy. Eris was immediately thrust into a grueling regimen that pushed her to her absolute limits.

From dawn to dusk, Eris swung her sword tirelessly. She sparred with other students, each bout a fierce battle that left her battered and bruised. She endured harsh criticism and demanding exercises, all designed to strip away her impulsive nature and forge her into a disciplined swordsmaster.

The transition was not easy for Eris. Used to relying on her raw talent and ferocious spirit, she struggled with the strict discipline and mental focus required by the Sword God Style. There were days when she questioned her decision, nights when she lay awake missing Rudeus and doubting her ability to reach his level.

But with each passing day, Eris's determination grew stronger. She channeled her frustrations and doubts into her training, pushing herself beyond what she thought possible. Slowly but surely, she began to see improvements. Her strikes became sharper, her movements more precise. She started to grasp the deeper philosophies behind the Sword God Style, learning to harness her fierce spirit into controlled, devastating techniques.

As the months turned into years, Eris's reputation within the Holy Land of Swords grew. She became known for her relentless training, often practicing long after others had retired for the day. Her sparring matches became events that other students gathered to watch, amazed by the raw power and growing finesse of her swordplay.

Throughout this time, thoughts of Rudeus remained her driving force. Every swing of her sword, every bruise endured, every small victory achieved was another step towards her goal of standing beside him as an equal. The promise of reunion kept her going through the toughest times, fueling her resolve to master the Sword God Style.

Little did Eris know that her journey was far from over. The path to becoming a Sword King would be long and fraught with challenges. But with each passing day, the wild, impulsive girl who had left Fittoa was being forged into a formidable warrior, one worthy of standing alongside the man she loved and facing whatever threats the world might throw their way.

Background Story for Eris Greyrat (Age 20)

Five years had passed since Eris Greyrat first set foot in the Holy Land of Swords, driven by an unwavering determination to become strong enough to stand beside Rudeus as an equal. Those years had transformed her from a talented but undisciplined swordswoman into a true master of the blade.

Under the rigorous tutelage of Sword God Gal Farion, Eris had honed her skills to a razor's edge. The Sword God Style, with its emphasis on overwhelming offensive power, suited her natural aggression and fighting spirit. She had learned to channel her fierce emotions into her swordplay, turning her once-uncontrolled outbursts into precisely executed techniques.

Eris's journey to mastery was not without its challenges. She faced numerous setbacks and moments of doubt, particularly when comparing herself to prodigies like Nina Farion, the Sword God's daughter. However, each obstacle only fueled her determination. She trained relentlessly, often pushing herself to the brink of exhaustion, driven by the memory of Rudeus and her promise to return to him.

Her dedication paid off. In a grueling series of trials and battles, Eris proved herself worthy of the title of Sword King. Her mastery of advanced techniques like the "Light Sword" and her ability to release controlled bursts of killing intent impressed even the stoic Gal Farion. When she was finally bestowed with the rank of Sword King, it was a moment of triumph tinged with the bittersweet knowledge that her time in the Holy Land of Swords was coming to an end.

As Eris prepared to leave, Gal Farion presented her with a final gift - a powerful sword befitting her new status. With this blade at her side and five years of intensive training behind her, Eris felt ready to face whatever challenges lay ahead.

However, her return to Rudeus's side was not as straightforward as she had imagined. Upon arriving at his home, Eris was confronted with a reality she hadn't fully prepared for - Rudeus had married twice in her absence. Sylphiette, his childhood friend, and Roxy, his former teacher, were now his wives.

This revelation shook Eris to her core. Despite her growth and maturity, she found herself grappling with intense emotions - jealousy, uncertainty, and fear that she might have lost her place in Rudeus's life. It was a testament to her growth that instead of lashing out as her younger self might have, she took time to process these feelings.

The situation came to a head when Rudeus prepared to face off against the Dragon God Orsted, the very being Eris had trained to defeat. Without hesitation, she rushed to his aid, her sword ready to protect the man she loved. In the heat of battle, fighting alongside Rudeus once again, Eris found clarity. She realized that her love for him hadn't diminished, and neither had his for her.

In the aftermath of the confrontation with Orsted, Eris and Rudeus finally had the opportunity to clear the air. Years of misunderstandings and unspoken feelings came to light. Eris learned that Rudeus had misinterpreted her departure years ago, thinking she had left because he wasn't good enough. In turn, she was able to express the depth of her feelings and the real reason behind her quest for strength.

With honesty and open hearts, they reconciled. Rudeus proposed to Eris, asking her to become his third wife. After some initial hesitation and discussions with Sylphiette and Roxy, Eris accepted, ready to take on this new challenge of being part of a complex family dynamic.

Adjusting to life as Rudeus's wife brought its own set of challenges for Eris. The skills that made her a formidable Sword King didn't always translate well to domestic life or the intricacies of noble society. She often felt out of her depth in social situations, struggling with etiquette and small talk. However, just as she had with her sword training, Eris approached these challenges with determination and a willingness to learn.

Her relationships with Sylphiette and Roxy evolved over time. Initial awkwardness gave way to mutual respect and eventually a deep bond. Eris found herself part of a unique family unit, each wife bringing their own strengths to support Rudeus and each other.

As she settled into her new life, Eris didn't abandon her martial pursuits. She took on the role of protector for the family, often accompanying Rudeus on dangerous missions. Her sword skills, honed to perfection in the Holy Land of Swords, proved invaluable in safeguarding their growing family.

The birth of her son, Ars, marked another significant change in Eris's life. Motherhood brought out a softer side of her, one that balanced her warrior's spirit with a fierce, protective love for her child. She found herself facing a new challenge - raising a child while maintaining her identity as a swordswoman and wife.

As she approached her twentieth year, Eris Greyrat had come a long way from the wild, uncontrollable girl she once was. She had achieved her goal of becoming strong enough to stand beside Rudeus, not just as a powerful ally in battle, but as an equal partner in life. The journey had been long and fraught with challenges, but Eris had emerged as a formidable Sword King, a loving wife, a protective mother, and a woman finally at peace with herself and her place in the world.
